senses.gloss:
रेशयदारिन् रेशय-दारिन् (रेशय = हिंसत्),
Ved. destroying those who injure, (used in Nirukta
VI. 14. to explain रिशादस्, q. v.)
रेशी रेशी, f., Ved. epithet of water.

रेष् 1. रेष्, cl. 1. A. रेषते, रिरेषे, रे-
षितुम्, to howl, roar, yell (as wolves); to
neigh, whinny (as a horse; cf. rt. ह्रेष्); to utter
any inarticulate sound.

2. रेष्, ट्, ट्, ट्, one who howls or neighs, howling,
neighing.

रेष् 3. रेष्, ट् (fr. rt. 1. रिष्), in Vājasa-
neyi-s. VI. 18. according to Mahī-dhara = रिष्टा or
हिंसिता, (perhaps referrible to rt. रिश्, to injure.)

1. रेषण, अम्, n. the howl of a wolf, howling,
yelling, roaring.
रेषा, f. howling, yelling (of wolves); neighing.
रेष, अस्, m., Ved. injury, hurt, receiving injury.

रेषित, अस्, आ, अम्, yelled, sounded; (अम्), n.
neighing, roaring.

रेषिन्, ई, इणी, इ, injuring, hurting; [cf. पुरु-
ष-र्˚.]

रेष्टृ, टा, ट्री, टृ, one who injures or hurts,
an injurer.

रेष्मन्, आ, m., Ved. a storm, whirlwind, storm-
cloud, (according to Mahī-dhara) the dissolution or
destruction of the world.
—रेष्म-च्छिन्न or
रेष्म-मथित, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. rent or broken
by a storm, torn up by a tempest.

रेष्म्य, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. being in or exposed to
a storm, involved in destruction (at the dissolution
of the world).
